goal: A step whose session dies because the machine restarted, the runner was killed, or macOS killed the session is never `failed` and never waits on a person. The runner itself resumes the same session when its prompt cache is warm or its conversation is small, and otherwise starts a fresh session on the same branch with the earlier session's work committed and a handover in its prompt.

After a restart the runner starts by itself at login when it was running when the machine went down, and it starts no new step while memory is short. The work a running session has not committed is snapshotted to a ref while it runs.

success_criteria.criterion: A step whose session pid is gone becomes `ready` with an `interrupted` record holding the session id, tool, log, last activity and context size, and is not `failed`.
success_criteria.check: `tests/mc/run.test.js`: a register with a `running` step whose pid is dead and a partial claude stream log, and one with a codex log; after `queue()` the step is `ready`, `interrupted.session_id` is the stream's id, `last_activity` is the log's mtime, `count` is 1. A third interruption in a row makes it `failed` with the reason naming three interruptions.

success_criteria.criterion: A warm or small interrupted session is resumed: the same session id continues, in the same worktree, with its uncommitted files untouched and without origin/main merged in first.
success_criteria.check: Live, once, in the close-out: while a step session runs, `mc run stop --force`, then `mc run start`; the step's next row in `~/mc/runner/log/runs.tsv` has the same `session` value as the killed one, and `git status --porcelain` in its workarea was not emptied by the runner. Also `tests/mc/run.test.js` for claude and `tests/mc/run-codex.test.js` for codex argument lists.

success_criteria.criterion: A cold, large interrupted session gets a fresh session on the same branch with the leftover files committed as one WIP commit and a handover paragraph in its prompt.
success_criteria.check: `tests/mc/run.test.js`: an interrupted record with `last_activity` two hours old and `context_tokens` 120 000 over a dirty worktree; the launch is not a resume, one commit `<project>: WIP left by an interrupted session` is made with `--no-verify`, and the prompt carries the handover with the commits and the last assistant text.

success_criteria.criterion: The runner starts at login when it was running when the machine went down, and not otherwise.
success_criteria.check: `tests/mc/run-control.test.js` for `--if-was-running` in the three states; `plutil -lint ~/Library/LaunchAgents/se.memoro.mc-runner.plist` passes after a `mc run start` on this machine.

success_criteria.criterion: No step starts while `kern.memorystatus_level` is under the floor, and the page says so, as it says the disk hold.
success_criteria.check: `tests/mc/run.test.js` with the memory reader stubbed under and at the floor; `tests/mc/status-collect.test.js` (or the test beside `nowBlock`) shows `disk` and `memory` in the RUNNER block's data.

success_criteria.criterion: While a step session runs, its uncommitted work is snapshotted to `refs/mc/checkpoint/<project>` without touching the worktree or its index, and before every `merge --abort` the runner makes.
success_criteria.check: `tests/mc/run.test.js` against a real temporary git repository: after a snapshot the ref's tree holds a modified and an untracked file, `git status --porcelain` is unchanged, and `git diff --cached` is empty.

steps.title: 1. The session log is written as it streams, and a dead session is interrupted, not failed
steps.done_when: A session's stdout reaches `<stem>.jsonl` as it arrives; the register's `session` carries `log`; `sweepRunning` and the post-session path turn a session that died under the step into `ready` with an `interrupted` record (session id, tool, model, log, last activity, context tokens, branch, count, at), `failed` only on the third in a row; `mc step <project>` prints the record; tests cover claude and codex logs; `npm test` is green.
comments: Interrupted record lives on the register step as `interrupted` (kept on ready/running, cleared otherwise); one helper `recordInterrupted` in run.js writes it for both sweepRunning and the signal case, and counts from the previous record. Live log: streamSession logPath = `${out}.jsonl`; session.log is the stem. docs/technical/mc-run.md still describes the old failed sweep — left for the close-out.

steps.title: 2. A warm or small interrupted session is resumed where it stopped
steps.done_when: `recoveryFor` decides resume or fresh from the record, the adapter's cache TTL and the context size; a resume launches the same session id through the tool's own resume with the workarea untouched (no dirty block, no branch move, no merge of main); a resume that cannot start falls back to fresh on the next pick; interrupted steps are picked first, warmest first; tests cover claude and codex; `npm test` is green.
comments: Resume path lives in run.js resumable() + recoveryFor (run-plan.js). When recoveryFor says fresh, resumable() returns null and the normal flow runs — a dirty interrupted workarea is still blocked dirty-worktree; step 3 hooks its WIP commit + handover there. resume_failed records go fresh; count is not bumped. Codex TTL 5 min equals WARM_MARGIN_MS, so codex is never warm — only cold-small resumes.

steps.title: 3. A cold, large interrupted session gets a fresh session with its leftovers committed and a handover
steps.done_when: When `recoveryFor` says fresh, the step's own leftover files are committed as one WIP commit on the step's branch before the usual flow, and `stepPrompt` carries a handover (why, the commits on the branch, the WIP commit, the last assistant text, the checkpoint ref if any); foreign dirt still blocks; tests cover it; `npm test` is green.
comments: Step 3 (#832): fresh recovery commits the interrupted session's own dirt (current branch = interrupted.branch, the project name, or <project>-*) as one --no-verify WIP commit, and the handover is built by handoverOf in run.js. The checkpoint ref is named only when rev-parse --verify finds refs/mc/checkpoint/<project>, so once step 6 writes that ref the handover names it with no further change. placeBranch's keepLocal stops a merger-returned branch being reset to origin over the unpushed WIP commit.

steps.title: 4. The runner starts at login when it was running when the machine went down
steps.done_when: `mc run start --if-was-running` starts a runner only when `runner.json` names a dead pid and no `STOP` is present, and otherwise prints why not and exits 0; every `mc run start` writes `~/Library/LaunchAgents/se.memoro.mc-runner.plist` (RunAtLoad, no KeepAlive) when its content differs; `mc run` help names the flag; tests cover the three states and the plist text; `npm test` is green.
comments: Login agent: plist written by every spawning start via deps.writeAgent (darwin only, on change). --if-was-running restarts with the dead runner's args from runner.json. Criterion 3's live half (plutil -lint on the real plist after a real mc run start) is left for the close-out; met stays false.

steps.title: 5. No step starts while memory is short, and the page shows both holds
steps.done_when: A pass starts no step while `kern.memorystatus_level` is under `MEMORY_MIN_FREE_PERCENT` (20), says `memory: <n>% free, below 20% — no step started` once per pass and writes `memory.json`; `nowBlock` reads `disk.json` and `memory.json` so the RUNNER block shows either hold; tests cover both; `npm test` is green.

steps.title: 6. A running session's uncommitted work is snapshotted to a ref
steps.done_when: Every `CHECKPOINT_MS` (10 min) while a step session runs, and before each `merge --abort` the runner makes in a step's workarea, a dirty worktree is snapshotted to `refs/mc/checkpoint/<project>` through a temporary index, with the worktree, the real index and HEAD untouched; the handover names the ref; tests against a real git repository; `npm test` is green.
comments: Snapshots go through checkpoint() in src/mc/checkpoint.js with GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0 and a temporary index at ~/mc/runner/scratch/checkpoint-<project>-<runner pid>.index. The runner snapshots every CHECKPOINT_MS and before all four merge --abort calls in runStepClaimed. The 10-minute timer itself was not run live.

steps.title: 7. Close-out
steps.done_when: The live resume check has been run and its runs.tsv rows quoted in this step's comments; every criterion is measured and marked; `docs/technical/mc-run.md` describes interrupted steps, resume and fresh recovery, the login agent, the memory hold and checkpoints; `docs/project/project_log.md` has the row; every step is `done` with its PR.
